01.note: The video starts with a recap of the earlier demo and the plan to finish the game. It gives no development time, no ROM size and no CPU name.

02.note: The video lists the work to do: graphics, world, music, a music engine, enemies, sound effects and cartridges. It does not follow nine stages.

03.note: The video says only that the game is written in pure assembly. It does not discuss compilers, an OS or a memory management unit.

04.note: The video puts the 192 x 168 tile world in the second RAM bank, 63 K. The maze comes from random rooms and tunnels to the closest connected room (24:26).

05.note: The video gives mode 1, layer 1 for the environment and layer 2 for the HUD. The packed BCD counters start at 31:44.

06.note: The video explains HDMA for the title screen clouds on layer 2, not for layer 3 in the game.

07.note: The video shows that transparent tile-zero sprites still count. The fix moves them off screen. Inkbox does not rotate sprite priority (30:08).

08.note: The video finds the tile under the player from X and Y with the scroll. It gives no formula, no complexity class and no spatial hash.

09.note: The video darkens layer 1 with black tiles on layer 3 and add-half color math. No subtraction, no inversion, no single-frame flash.

10.note: The audio part runs from here to 19:30. Five voices play music, and three dedicated voices wait for sound effects (18:18).

11.note: The video shows the transparent cartridge parts and solder paste. It shows no ROM flashing, no console test and no emulator comparison.

12.note: The video does not give a stage table. The subsystems exist in the video, but the challenge and solution cells repeat the errors of parts 04 to 11.

13.note: The video gives the three memories: CPU 128 K, PPU 64 K, APU 64 K. The diagram adds layer, voice and inversion details that the video does not give.

14.note: The video moves the objects out of bank $7F into the first bank to avoid bank register swaps. Tunnels are thin rooms (25:50), not single tiles.

15.note: The video says that BCD makes the math easier and that INC and DEC ignore the decimal flag. It does not say that the CPU lacks division.

16.note: The video writes the layer 2 horizontal scroll register from a three-byte HDMA table on the title screen. The scanline bands in this part are not in the video.

17.note: The video gives the 34-sliver rule: only 17 of 24 objects drew. No vertical sort and no priority cycling.

18.note: The video says that a tile lookup is faster than a loop over a wall list. The address formula and the shift formula are not in the video, and the shift formula is wrong.

19.note: Hit stop pauses the game a few frames and darkens the background with the add-half trick. Talisman colors are four palette colors of one cloud (42:39).

20.note: The video assigns voices 0 to 4 to music and the last three to sound effects on standby. No voice is taken from the music.

21.note: The video does not cover this idea. The cartridge is not finished in the video (46:55), and no hardware test or emulator divergence is shown.

22.note: The video does not give a budget matrix. The CPU has hardware multiply and divide registers, which this part denies.

23.note: The video does not cover this idea. It does not discuss compilers or register files.

24.note: The video ends with the free release, a poll about a physical release, and the next console. It does not claim 9,999 floors.

25.note: The video does not cover this idea. The citations point to a news article, not to the video.
